svg.title: The merged capability catalog, and the one name that collides
svg.desc: On the left a table lists the five names the model is offered, the client each one resolves to, and the name that is actually sent on the wire. Three rows, read_file, fetch_page and run_query, are identical in both name columns because those names were already unique. Two rows are tinted and marked renamed: files dot search and docs dot search both go out on the wire as plain search. On the right, three server cards show what each server exposes, with the two search entries tinted and marked as exported by two servers. A note explains that the prefix comes from the key you gave each connection in configuration and never from the name a server reports for itself, and that the server has never heard of the qualified form.
svg.text: The host merges every list into one map. Only a contested name gets qualified.
the flat list the model is offered
Three of these five names were already unique across every
connected server, so they come through untouched. Only search
was contested, so the host qualified it on both sides, using the
key you gave each connection in your own configuration file.
The prefix never comes from the name a server
reports for itself. That one is not guaranteed
The right-hand column is what actually leaves
the host. The server has never heard of
